checks.label: The selected patients are Flu patients
Clinical staff are with Flu patients
Flu patients include new arrivals

limits: The action admits the whole represented arrival cohort rather than an individually chosen quantity.
The action does not update bed counters because the hospital is not an action participant.
The action does not refuse admission for insufficient beds; resulting overcapacity must be interpreted from represented totals.
mechanics.rationale: Clinical staff admit the currently represented daily arrivals into the represented hospitalized population. Bed availability is not changed because the hospital is not an action participant.
semantic_bindings: patients denotes the represented Flu patients population
new_arrivals_per_day is treated as the current arrival cohort
tests: Clinical staff at the same location can admit Flu patients when represented arrivals are positive.
The action is refused when the selected reference is not the participating Flu patients.
The action is refused when Clinical staff and Flu patients are at different locations.
The action is refused when no new arrivals are represented.
A successful admission adds the arrival count to hospitalized patients and clears the represented arrivals.

checks.label: The selected patients are Flu patients
The selected equipment is Ventilators
Clinical staff are with Flu patients
Clinical staff are with Ventilators
Flu patients include someone waiting for ventilation
Ventilators include an available unit

limits: Each action allocates exactly one ventilator.
The action relies on patients_waiting_for_ventilation to represent the patients currently requiring allocation.
Hospital ventilator counters are synchronized later by an autonomous process rather than changed directly.
mechanics.rationale: Clinical staff assign one represented available ventilator to one represented patient waiting for ventilation, updating both population and equipment stocks.
semantic_bindings: patients_waiting_for_ventilation is demand eligible for allocation
one allocation moves one patient and one ventilator between corresponding stocks
tests: Clinical staff can allocate one available Ventilators unit to a waiting Flu patient at the shared location.
The action is refused when no Flu patient is waiting for ventilation.
The action is refused when no Ventilators unit is available.
The action is refused for mismatched patient or ventilator references.
A successful allocation transfers one unit from available to in use and one patient from waiting to on ventilation.

checks.label: The selected patients are Flu patients
The selected equipment is Ventilators
Clinical staff are with Flu patients
Clinical staff are with Ventilators
Flu patients include someone on ventilation
Ventilators include a unit in use
Flu patients include someone requiring ventilation

limits: Each action releases exactly one ventilator.
The action represents release only when ventilation need ends; it does not itself classify the patient as recovering or deceased.
Hospital ventilator counters are synchronized later by an autonomous process.
mechanics.rationale: Clinical staff release one ventilator from the represented patients, reducing active ventilation need and returning the same equipment unit to availability.
semantic_bindings: patients_on_ventilators and number_in_use are paired active-use stocks
release ends one represented ventilation requirement
the released operational unit returns to number_available
tests: Clinical staff can release one in-use Ventilators unit from Flu patients at the shared location.
The action is refused when no Flu patient is on ventilation.
The action is refused when no Ventilators unit is in use.
The action is refused when the selected references do not match the represented stocks.
A successful release reduces both active ventilation counts and makes one ventilator available.

checks.label: The selected supplier is Medical supplier
Clinical staff can contact Medical supplier here
The requested quantity is positive

limits: Only the listed positive order quantities are supported.
Submitting an order does not reserve supplier inventory or guarantee delivery.
The hospital pending-order count cannot be updated because the hospital is not an action participant.
The represented model does not retain supplier-specific order linkage or delivery age.
mechanics.rationale: Clinical staff submit a positive order quantity to the represented medical supplier, accumulating the quantity in the represented submitted-order count.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the number of ventilators requested
orders_submitted is the accumulated represented requested quantity
supplier identifies the intended medical supplier
tests: Clinical staff can submit each listed positive quantity to Medical supplier at the shared location.
The action is refused for a different supplier reference.
The action is refused when Clinical staff and Medical supplier are at different locations.
Zero and negative quantities are refused.
Submitting an order increases orders_submitted without consuming supplier inventory.

checks.label: Medical supplier is the selected supplier
The selected supplier is Medical supplier
The selected destination is Hospital
Medical supplier can dispatch to Hospital here
The dispatch quantity is positive
The dispatch fits Medical supplier's daily limit
Medical supplier has the dispatched ventilators

limits: Only the listed quantities can be dispatched, and each dispatch cannot exceed maximum_delivery_per_day.
The inventory check prevents dispatching equipment that is not represented in supplier stock.
Delivery delay is not modeled because no represented shipment or activity state can retain elapsed delivery time.
Dispatch is not matched against an individual order because no shared order reference is represented.
The co-located Ventilators stock is synchronized from Hospital counters by an autonomous process.
mechanics.rationale: The medical supplier dispatches an allowed positive quantity from represented inventory to the represented hospital, where it increases ventilator capacity and availability.
semantic_bindings: supplier inventory is the source stock
hospital ventilator capacity and availability are the destination stocks
tests: Medical supplier can dispatch an allowed quantity from sufficient inventory to Hospital.
The action is refused when the acting supplier differs from the selected supplier.
The action is refused for a different hospital reference.
The action is refused when quantity exceeds maximum_delivery_per_day or represented inventory.
A successful dispatch lowers supplier inventory and raises Hospital ventilator capacity and availability by the same quantity.

checks.label: The selected patients are Flu patients
Clinical staff are with Flu patients
The recorded status is recovering
Flu patients include a hospitalized patient not on ventilation

limits: Each action records exactly one recovering patient.
The deceased status is not supported by this mechanic because one action definition cannot conditionally select different numeric counters from the status string.
A patient still represented as using a ventilator must have that ventilator released separately.
Hospital bed counters cannot be changed because the hospital is not an action participant.
mechanics.rationale: Clinical staff record one represented hospitalized Flu patient as recovering, moving one patient from the hospitalized count to the recovering count.
semantic_bindings: status is conservatively restricted to recovering
tests: Clinical staff can record one non-ventilated hospitalized Flu patient as recovering.
The action is refused for a status other than recovering, including deceased.
The action is refused when no hospitalized patient outside the ventilated group is represented.
The action is refused for a mismatched patient reference or location.
A successful record decreases hospitalized_patients and increases patients_recovering by one.

checks.label: Flu patients have no unadmitted arrivals

processes.rationale: After the represented arrival cohort has been admitted and cleared, the next round supplies a new cohort at the world's represented daily arrival level.

checks.label: Medical supplier has a positive replenishment rate

processes.rationale: The supplier receives continuing upstream replenishment each round at its represented maximum daily delivery rate, preventing the ongoing supply chain from permanently running down.
Hospital ventilator counters and the co-located Ventilators stock are two represented views of the same equipment, so the detailed stock follows the hospital view each round.
